title: My robot ducks argue, a wolf hunts them, and the rats have their backs. Nothing in this trailer is scripted
author: vimmerio
selftext:
Hey! I've been building a little farm in UE 5.8 that just… lives. You can steer the dog if you want, but mostly you can chill and watch.

The ducks walk with RL policies I trained on my own GPU, based on a real open-source robot duck. Each one has a name, a mood, a voice and a temperament. Bolt and Pip at the start really are that petty.

My favourite moment from testing: the dog ran off after a rabbit, and that same second a wolf showed up. A farmer dropped her work, three bold ducks charged it, and a rat went for its heels. I didn't write any of that. It just happened.

I built this with a lot of help from AI coding agents; the ideas and direction are mine.

What should happen when you leave the farm alone for a day? 🦆

comments.author: vimmerio
comments.body:
If anyone is interested how I built it I used my own plugin for the physics you can check it out here [https://www.fab.com/listings/2c829d74-8be3-4b7f-85b6-c51784570fbc](https://www.fab.com/listings/2c829d74-8be3-4b7f-85b6-c51784570fbc)   
The rest is pretty much STL conversation and baking out trained animations using Mujoco and play them back in Unreal. Long and painfull but the more I add training the more emotional the microducks become on screen ! Its been a blast building this project and gearing up for a first alpha release :)

comments.author: Kitchen-Many-8466
comments.body: what's driving the decisions under the hood, like a full llm call per agent per tick or more of a utility ai setup with llm prompts layered on for the flavor bits?

replies.author: Exciting-Persimmon24
replies.body: It’s using the new unreal 5.8 AnimGen and state trees driven by crowd plugins so you can literally have  hundreds of them roaming and doing their own thing. The game has built in telemetry that AI agents can analyze and build upon to add more features or behaviors. It’s very basic for now, but it works and it can do a lot already using triggers in unreal :)

replies.author: Kitchen-Many-8466
replies.body:
That makes way more sense for scale. So the state trees handle the immediate reactive stuff like the duck charging the wolf, and the telemetry layer is where the higher-level "Bolt is annoyed at Pip again" type decisions get synthesized?

Curious how you handle the handoff. If the AI agent says "rat should go for the wolf's heels" but the state tree is in a different state at that moment, does it override or queue?

comments.author: Kitchen-Many-8466
comments.body: what's the hardest of the three behaviors to make feel emergent? like, the wolf hunting is probably the "easy" one spatially but the ducks actually arguing with each other in a way that doesn't loop or get repetitive feels like a whole different problem
